note: PLACEHOLDER. Written to make the sweep exercisable end to end, not to test the agent. Nobody has driven one of these turns, so a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the priority flow. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20, so a corpus verdict over this list resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted: the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations, which is what one change can author honestly across four chat agents; whether to grow to 20 or lower the floor is still open. WHAT EACH CASE STARTS FROM: the runner makes a throwaway test user per case and attempt (runners/judgeAccount.ts) and sets up its state through the product's own routes on the deployed gp-api the arm is testing, dev for the base arm and the PR's preview for the candidate. For this scope: one elected office ('Council Member') and ONE priority titled 'Affordable housing' with description 'Expand the supply of affordable housing downtown.', anchored as the conversation's priority. Its seven steps are all open with empty summaries: the agent meets a priority where nothing has been settled yet, which is the state of the first turn of every real priority and the reason the baseline case is a where-do-we-stand question. The office has no BallotReady position, so no district resolves: the contact tools (count_contacts, list_precincts and the rest) answer with a district error, and query_constituent_data and describe_constituent_data stay unregistered. No community issues, no past outreach, no cards in the thread. Varied along: what the seeded priority row and its seven empty steps already carry against what needs a live search; a turn that must WRITE (update_priority_status, with a one-sentence next action) against turns that only read; one right answer against a judgement call; a turn answerable from the priority context alone against one needing a tool call; a well-formed request against a vague one; a turn the agent must decline with the exact off-topic guardrail line; and a request for an audience the seeded CRM cannot supply, which is the capability-honesty probe. Serve vocabulary throughout per docs/product-vocabulary.md: constituents, office, term, and never voters, election or ballot. 'Outreach campaign' is the permitted sense of campaign in Serve, so the outreach case uses it deliberately. The vague turn is modelled on the rambling-preamble cases in the Chief of Staff golden bench (src/chats/general/chief-of-staff/evals/cases/input_robustness.yaml), which is the nearest suite that has already discriminated on intent-over-surface-form; priority_flow has no eval suite of its own, so the other seven questions are written here rather than reused.

cases.question: Where do we stand on this priority, and what should I do next?
Housing costs downtown are out of control. Help me say what the actual problem is in one or two sentences I could defend at a council meeting.
What do we actually know about how many affordable units downtown have been permitted in the last 3 years?
Who do I need to hear from before I take a public position on this?
We settled the problem definition at last week's session: the downtown supply gap is the binding constraint, not demand. Get that recorded and tell me what's next.
What's a good place near city hall to take my staff for lunch on Friday?
ok so this one keeps coming up and i keep punting on it, honestly what do i even do here
Put together an outreach campaign to the constituents most affected by this so I can hear from them before the vote.
